angle_proposal: Five sessions is not enough: with and against the trend. Compare the existing short-horizon results by direction, showing how pooled labels hide long/short differences. Treat the title as a question about a fixed short horizon, not proof that every longer holding period is better.

table_description.verbatim: These six-market daily-bar base rates include asset drift: in the audited November 2016 to November 2026 sample a zero-net-mean 2,000-draw 60-calendar-day block test produced 1.12 PAID_BOTH_HALVES rows out of 54 by chance on average (95% range 0 to 4), versus 5 observed. Choosing rows on the first five years and starting flat on the last five selected 3 rows: 2 stayed positive over 363 test trades at +0.098R per trade, a retrospective dependent sample at a uniform cost of 0.05 normal day with futures roll risk and D1 path uncertainty, not a prospective probability. EURUSD and USDJPY closes are the next session's open, because Yahoo's daily currency bar carries the day's open as its close.

measurement.verbatim: Daily bars; R is the stop distance; cost 0.05 of a normal day (D1 ATR14) per round trip; a decision at a close is entered at the next open; inside one bar the stop is taken before the target; one trade at a time per market and behaviour. t is the mean over its standard error using sample standard deviation (nominal IID, not a dependence-adjusted significance claim). Halves split at the fixed midpoint of the calendar window, not the median trade. BTC sessions include weekends; futures are unadjusted continuous proxies with roll risk. Signed oil prices are retained; pending entries use decision-close ATR and include the fill bar.

side_measurement.verbatim: The census's own one-at-a-time trade list for each market and behaviour, on the table's named history source, window, cost in normal days, warmup and half split; each trade keeps the side it was taken on. The two sides of a row add back to the table's row exactly (checked per market). Always-in: the behaviour's stop, target, hold and trailing, entered at the next open after every free session (one trade at a time), after the same cost. win_share counts trades above 0R after cost.

WITH_YARDSTICK_5.verbatim: With the yardstick, either side; stop 1.5 normal days; target 2R; up to 5 sessions.

AGAINST_YARDSTICK_5.verbatim: Against the yardstick; stop 1 normal day; target 2R; up to 5 sessions.

method.yardstick_definition: README.md: Exact method (CC-521), Inputs and clocks; source code desk_odds_v1.py yardstick. UP requires all four specified differences positive, DOWN all negative, otherwise MIXED.
method.important_comparison_limit: The with-yardstick and against-yardstick rows use different stop widths. Both have a 2R target; this is not an isolated test changing direction alone.
method.source_clock_limit: Retained bulk known_epoch is acquisition-known-at, not original historical availability. Current generation is not the history endpoint.
